ai.description: This frog reaches 30–40 mm. It is brown with a dark lateral band and a white belly. Distinctive features include a pointed snout, long slender limbs, and prominent dorsolateral folds.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Walkerana leptodactyla* is best distinguished by its distinct, prominent dorsolateral folds that extend from behind the eyes to the groin, which are absent in similar species.
ai.habitat: *Walkerana leptodactyla* inhabits the leaf litter and rocky stream banks of evergreen forests in the Western Ghats, typically at elevations between 800 and 1,500 meters.
ai.behavior: Walkerana leptodactyla is primarily nocturnal, often found leaping into nearby streams or hiding under leaf litter when disturbed to evade potential predators.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Walkerana leptodactyla* breeds during the monsoon, laying clutches of 30–50 eggs in mossy, semi-aquatic habitats. Its development is direct, bypassing the tadpole stage.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Walkerana leptodactyla* is endemic to the Western Ghats of India, primarily occurring in the states of Kerala and Tamil Nadu at elevations between 800 and 1,800 meters.
ai.callDescription: The advertisement call of *Walkerana leptodactyla* consists of a series of high-pitched, insect-like chirps, typically heard near fast-flowing forest streams.
